   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, December 2, 2024

1.  WELCOME AND CALL TO ORDER

  Chairperson Walters called the meeting to order at 8:34 a.m. The following Board
  Members were present: Craig Walters, Marianne Stark, Micky Rehm, Zuhey Espinoza
  and George Henderson. City Representatives present: Community Development Director
  Eric Scherer, Council Member Steve Johnson, and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others
  present: Nathan Ulsh, Maria Faura, Amanda Reifel, Jeff Nasmyth, Mike McAdams,
  Alexanda Bautista-Abad, Luz Bautista-Abad, Wendy Norton, Ken Valmonte, and Fang
  Wang.

2.  CALENDAR
  Holiday Stroll  Saturday, December 7th 3pm
  Wine Walk  Saturday, April 26th 5pm-8:30pm

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

  It was moved by Ms. Stark and seconded by Ms. Rehm to approve the minutes of the
  October 7, 2024 and October 29, 2024 meetings. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Halloween and Cruisin La Verne Recaps – The Board agreed that the Halloween
  event was well attended.

  Mr. Scherer stated that this was the last holiday car show under the current
  agreement. The car show was better attended and more cars participated. Mr.
  Nasmyth of Fourth Street Mill stated that the event attendees did not spill over to
  their location.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  Holiday Stroll Update – The carolers will be present from 3:30-6pm, Santa is
  confirmed, and Ms. Rehm is purchasing the candy canes. Mr. Walter will be the
  point person the day of the event.

  B.  BID Evaluation Consultant Update – Mr. Ulsh stated that he is working with the
  University on a business partnership. There is still two months left in the review,
  and he will provide a presentation at the annual meeting scheduled for February 3,
  2025.

  Mr. Scherer asked the restaurant owners present to stay after the meeting to have
  further discussion.
 6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer): Mr. Scherer stated that the Outdoor Dining Policy would
  be discussed at the next regular meeting and the policy would be presented to City
  Council on January 20, 2025.
  B. University Report (Zuhey Espinoza): Dr. Espinoza stated that they hosted a voting
  center on campus, and two weeks ago they offered legal services. Forbes also
  recognized the University’s Doctorate Program and Upward Mobility Program.
  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm stated that the Holiday Stroll postcard was
  mailed.
  D. Chamber Report: Ms. Stark stated that Chamber Holiday Luncheon is December 12th
  at Café Wang.
  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): Mr. Walters stated that the website is being
  updated to include background and history of Old Town, an updated calendar,
  business directory, and events.
  F. Financial Report: None

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Mr. Ulsh stated that he met with the University twice to discuss a partnership and has had
  conversations with the businesses. Some of the items discussed included parking, an art
  commission and beatification, and welcome points at the entrances of Old Town.

  The Board discussed the art style, entry points, a directory, and parking. Dr. Espinoza
  stated that there are pay lots near Mainiero Square.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:23 a.m., the regular meeting to be held on January 6, 2025 at
  8:30 a.m. at Café Wang – 2316 D Street, La Verne CA 91750

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie Hiatt

RE: DRAFT Incidental Outdoor Sidewalk Dining and Furniture Policy

Dear Business Owner:

As you may be aware, the City had previously established a policy regulating the placement of
tables and chairs and other displays within the public right-of-way, or sidewalk areas. This policy
was put into place just before the Covid pandemic and was never fully implemented. As the City
has taken a hands-off approach for the last several years regarding items on the sidewalk in Old
Town, we are looking to update and re-establish this policy.

Attached is the DRAFT policy outlining what is permitted and the steps to obtain the necessary
permits moving forward. Businesses would be allowed to have two tables and four chairs or 6
square feet of display area within the sidewalk area with certain rules related to access,
maintenance, and insurance requirements. Request for more space can be considered but would
result in a lease agreement with the City to occupy that space.

We are currently reviewing lease rates for outdoor space and discussing the terms of any such
agreement moving forward. More information on these aspects will be shared at a future date.

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District Advisory Board will be discussing
this draft policy at their next meeting on Monday, January 6, 2025 at 8:30 am at Café Wang
(2316 D St.) where you are welcome to attend and provide input. The Board will be asked to
make a recommendation on this policy to the City Council, who is expected to discuss the policy at
their meeting on Tuesday January 21, 2025 at 6:30 pm at City Hall.

Provided that the policy is approved, City staff will work with businesses to ensure compliance,
with the goal of have any lease agreements in place and to become effective on July 1, 2025.

Hard copies of this letter and the draft policy will be delivered to those businesses that currently
have items within the sidewalk area and those that use other City property for outdoor dining
purposes on Thursday December 26th.

Sincerely

Eric Scherer, AICP
Community Development Director

  PARKLETS INFORMATION
  Submittal Requirements
PURPOSE

The City of La Verne has launched the La Verne Incidental Outdoor Dining/Decorative Furniture Permit
Program to help local businesses and the community further utilize public property to facilitate positive
activity such as outdoor dining and shopping.

This portion of the program allows for the use of the parking lane and sidewalk for business
operations, like seating, dining operations, or merchandising for businesses by the construction of a
parklet or on designated sidewalk areas.

Parklets repurpose part of the street adjacent to the sidewalk into a public space. While they are funded
and maintained by the businesses and property owner, they are publicly accessible and open to all.

Parklets are only intended to be installed on low-speed streets regardless of the barrier system installed.
No sidewalk or on-street dining shall occur on roadways with speed limits above 25 mph.

The safety of patrons, employees and other street users are paramount. Additionally, these parklets must
be accessible to all as required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

Property owners may apply and must comply with all of the program requirements or face revocation of
permission to participate in the program.
PROCESS

  1. Prepare a Proposal per the requirements listed in the Requirements section.
  a. Complete the La Verne Outdoor Dining/Merchandising Permit Application.
  b. Complete an Encroachment Permit Application
  c. Provide an initial site plan. This site plan must be to-scale and can be hand drawn.
  d. If available, provide photos of the location where you would like to install the parklet,
  including parking spaces, the sidewalk and building façade in front of the proposed
  location.
  i. If proposing sidewalk dining, prepare a site plan which contains the sidewalk and
  building façade in front of the proposed location.
  e. Provide proof of insurance with the City of La Verne named as additionally insured.
  f. Provide signed Hold Harmless Agreement.
  g. Provide signed Installation and Maintenance Agreement.
  h. You are strongly encouraged to inform nearby property owners and businesses regarding
  your intention to propose a parklet.
  2. Submit the proposal to the Planning Department.
  3. Proposal Review and Selection.
  4. Permits Issuance.

REQUIREMENTS

SITE PLAN

The initial site plan must show the existing street, sidewalk environment, the proposed parklet, dining
area, or merchandising area footprint and all street and sidewalk elements at least 20 feet on either side
of the proposed location. Site plans must be drawn to scale and may be hand drawn, as long as it is
legible and includes the following elements.

  •  Your building and adjacent properties (include addresses) and their building entrances
  •  Existing sidewalk width(s)
  •  Existing curb cuts and driveways
  •  Adjacent bicycle lane or auto traffic lane
  •  Existing parking spaces with dimensions
  •  Other existing sidewalk features near the proposed parklet area (e.g. fire hydrants, streetlights
  planters, bicycle racks, etc.)
  •  Existing utility valves and panels in the street and on the sidewalk
  •  All color curb zones (red, yellow, green, white and blue)
  •  Existing street trees and tree wells.
  •  Proposed parklet footprint and dimensions
  •  Parklet setback dimensions

If submitting for a parklet proposal, applicant shall submit plans that have been stamped by a
licensed civil engineer.

PARKLET LOCATION CRITERIA
Parklets are situated along the curbside on streets where on-street parking spaces exist. They can be
considered in any location where there are or would be space(s) for on street parallel, angled, or
perpendicular parking, including spaces with metered or unmetered parking.
Parallel Parking. Most parklets are the length of one or two parking spaces, although the City will
consider larger parklets depending on neighborhood and site conditions. A 4 ft. inner buffer is required
when adjacent to another parallel parking space (2 ft. when adjacent to a driveway, motorcycle/scooter
parking, or a bicycle corral).
Perpendicular and diagonal parking. Parklets located in perpendicular or diagonal parking spaces are
typically designed to be the size of three or more combined parking spaces to maximize habitable space
within the parklet. The edge of the parklet must be set back 3 ft. from the adjacent parking space on
either side.
Areas without marked parking spaces. In areas where parking spaces are not marked on the
pavement, the proposed parklet shall not leave an “orphaned” space that is too small to use as a full
parking space.
Corner locations. Parklets should be located at least one parallel parking space (20 ft.) away from an
intersection or street corner. Parklets closer to the corner may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Near crosswalks. Parklets need to be a minimum of 20 ft. from a crosswalk.

HEALTH
All businesses must comply with all State and City health requirements.

CONSENT
Parklet proposals are required to be signed by the property owner of the business establishment.
Proposals are also required to include a letter of consent or support from any adjacent businesses.

INSURANCE AND INDEMNIFICATION
All business owners are required to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless City of La Verne provide an
acceptable General Liability Insurance Certificate providing evidence of general liability insurance
coverage in the minimum amount of $1 million per occurrence, $2 million aggregate AND an additional
insured endorsement naming the City of La Verne, its officers, employees, and agents’ as additional
insured; all businesses also required to provide a primary/non-contributory endorsement and waiver of
subrogation in favor of the City of La Verne. Restaurants serving alcohol on public sidewalks and/or
public parking spaces shall also provide $1 million liquor liability insurance naming the City of La Verne,
its officers, employees, and agents’ as additional insured.

CONSTRUCTION
Parklets must:
  o Create a protective barrier on all three sides of the seating perimeter that are in the roadway, to
  separate seating from the travel lane. Barriers shall be crash-rated and determined
  acceptable by the City Engineer.
  o If utilizing K-rails, K-rails shall be enclosed to ensure a combability with design for the
  surrounding area. Exposed K-rails shall not be permitted.
  o The width of the outdoor dining/seating area shall not exceed the width of the frontage of the
  establishment. Units with multiple frontages may utilize two of their frontages for outdoor dining
  and shall be limited to the width of each of the frontages.
  o Ensure visibility of patrons and barriers at night by clearly marking all barriers with high intensity
  retro-reflective tape or reflectors of high visibility-colors and materials.
  o Comply with all ADA requirements such as:
  o Provide a ramp for ADA compliance, which can be made of nonpermanent materials.
  (e.g. wood, metal plate, etc.)
  o Provide an accessible path of travel of minimum of 48 inches wide for a maximum length
  of 200 feet on the sidewalk and does not pass over tree wells. The path of travel must be
  a minimum of 36 inches wide on the parklet deck surface.
  o Provide a dining table reserved for ADA on the sidewalk or parklet.
  o Not place seating or barriers within 15’ of a fire hydrant.
  o Not place seating or barriers within 20’ of a crosswalk to provide for safe vehicle turns
  and avoid crowding.
  o Not provide lighting that creates glare to passing traffic.
  o Not place seating within a red, blue or yellow curb zone, bike lane, or bus lane.
  o Not block rainwater drainage flowing along the curb through the gutter area and catch
  basin.
  o Any umbrellas to be installed shall have a minimum height of 7 feet from the floor surface. All
  umbrellas shall be compliant to wind and weight ratings.
  o Outdoor dining shall not inhibit vehicular or pedestrian circulation.
  o Awnings, covers, furniture, umbrellas, shade structures, or other physical elements shall be
  compatible with the character of the main structure and regularly maintained in good working
  order. Faded and ripped fabric and materials shall be replaced.

After construction, you must schedule a final inspection with the Building and Safety Inspector.

MAINTENANCE
Owners must submit a signed Maintenance Agreement with the City of La Verne. Business
establishments must use the following Best Management Practices for maintenance:
□ Remove litter/debris on and adjacent to the parklet daily
□ Remove litter/debris from under the parklet platform, including the gutter weekly or as needed
□ Clean surfaces (e.g. sweeping, power washing/hosing) weekly or as needed
□ Comply with Fats, Oils, Grease (FOG) Requirements

FIRE DEPARTMENT

All Fire Department requirements shall comply with the California Fire Code and requires the Fire
Marshal’s approval.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS
The applicant must demonstrate any other applicable conditions deemed necessary by the Director of
Community Development or the Community Development Director’s designee.

References
Please see the National Association of City Transportation Officials (NACTO) Urban Street Design Guide
for Parklets for more information: https://nacto.org/publication/urbanstreet‐design-guide/interim‐design‐
strategies/parklets/

  OLD TOWN LA VERNE SIDEWALK USE REQUIREMENTS
A. All outdoor uses permitted by this program shall be subject to the following standards:
B. A minimum two-foot clear space shall be maintained from the edge of the street curb or parking
  area.
C. A continuous path, not including the required two-foot clear space from street curb or parking
  area, shall be maintained for pedestrian traffic. In Old Town La Verne, a continuous path shall
  consist of two blocks worth (Exhibit B) Such path shall have a vertical clearance of not less than
  eight feet above the surface of the path.
D. All sidewalk use areas shall be continuously supervised by management or employees of the
  business to which they are connected to ensure required pathways are kept clear.
E. All sidewalk use areas shall be maintained in a clean and safe manner.
F. All items placed in the sidewalk area shall be maintained in good repair, and no item may be
  hazardous to pedestrian or vehicular traffic or extend into the safe line-of-sight distances at
  intersections, as determined by the City Engineer.
G. All entrances and emergency exits shall be kept clear.
H. No item placed in the sidewalk shall have a vertical height of more than six feet above the surface
  of the sidewalk, except as specifically approved by staff.
I.  All items placed in the sidewalk shall be removed each evening, unless otherwise approved by
  staff.
J.  There shall be a minimum of 36 inches of clearance between separate tables and chairs (Exhibit
  A)
K. All signage must comply with Title 17 of the La Verne Municipal Code.
L. If sidewalk use is to be located on private property; the business owner shall obtain prior
  authorization from the owner or management company of such property.
M. If a sidewalk use is to be located within the public right-of-way; the business owner shall first
  obtain an encroachment permit from the Public Works Department and provide the City with a
  certificate of insurance of general commercial liability insurance for an amount as required by the
  Director, naming the City as an additional insured. Such insurance shall be placed with a
  company satisfactory to the Director.
N. No services shall be provided outdoors in conjunction with any outdoor use, except for table
  service of food or other outdoor services (e.g. Hair, Nails, etc.) approved by Staff, in conjunction
  with approved outdoor seating.

O. No outdoor storage other than chairs and tables shall be permitted in conjunction with any
  outdoor use.
P. The width of the outdoor dining/seating area shall not exceed the width of the frontage of the
  establishment. Units with multiple frontages may utilize two of their frontages for outdoor dining
  and shall be limited to the width of each of the frontages.
Q. The pedestrian path shall be measured from the dining area boundary to the back of curb and
  other obstructions (e.g. planters, utility boxes).
R. Awnings, covers, furniture, umbrellas, shade structures, or other physical elements shall be
  compatible with the character of the main structure and regularly maintained in good working
  order. Faded and ripped fabric and materials shall be replaced.
S. Awnings, umbrellas, and similar covers must allow vertical clearance of seven feet above
  sidewalk level and shall provide coverage of the dining area only and maintain a two-foot
  horizontal clearance from pedestrian walkways.

OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, January 6,2025

I.  WELCOME ATID CALL TO ORDER

  Ms. Stark called the meeting to order at 8:33 a.m. The following Board Members were
  present: Marianne Stark, Micky Rehm, and Zuhey Espinoza. City Representatives
  present: Community Development Director Eric Scherer, Sr. Management Analyst
  Nicole Houston, Mayor Tim Hepbum, Mayor Pro Tem Steve Johnson, and Secretary
  Natalie Hiatt. Others present: Luz Bautista-Abad, Roberta Virgin, Francisco Ramirez,
  Ken Valmonte, Lori Alvarez, Lily Brainard, Shelby Califaux, and Fang Wang.

2.  CALENDAR
  Annual Meeting  Monday, February 3'd 8am
  Cool Cruise  Saturday, April 19th 10am-4pm
  Wine Walk  Saturday, April 26th 5pm-8:30pm

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES

  It was moved by Dr. Espinoza and seconded by Ms. Rehm to approve the minutes of the
  December 2,2024 meeting. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Introduction of Nicole Houston - Ms. Houston of the Public Works Department is
  the new contact for environmental programs.
  B.  Outdoor Sidewalk and Fumiture Policy - Mr. Scherer discussed the draft policy
  which would be effective July 1, 2025. The policy includes a two-tier rental rate.
  The higher rate would be applied to the businesses selling alcohol. Ms. Alvarez
  recommended that a limit be placed on the number of spaces per block. Mr.
  Scherer recommended limiting the percentage rather than a number limit.

  It was moved by Ms. Stark and seconded by Ms. Rehm to recommend only a
  maximum of 20 percent of parking on each side of the street to be occupied, per
  block and per side of the street. The motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

  C.  Holiday Stroll Recap - The Board received good feedback. Ms. Stark
  recommended that next year a portion of the lot be blocked off by Blading Ink to
  draw more activity to that end of the street. Mr. Scherer stated that the event could
  be moved to the second Saturday in December to reduce conflict with the San
  Dimas event.

  D.  Holiday Decorations for Mainiero Square - Mr. Scherer stated that there is $1,000
  of unused funds available if the Board wants to purchase more decorations for
  Mainiero Square. Ms. Rhem indicated that she would shop for decorations.
 5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  BID Evaluation Consultant Update - Mr. Scherer stated that staff will review the
  draft 5-year plan and will share it with everyone once it has been updated. A
  presentation of the draft plan will be given at the annual meeting and then
  formally present to the Board at their March meeting.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A. City Report (Eric Scherer):None
  B. University Report (Zvhey Espinoza): Dr. Espinoza asked if the Chamber is
  coordinating the State of the City at ULV. Ms. Califaux will follow up with more
  information.
  C. Marketing (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm suggested selling Wine Walk tickets at the Cool
  Cruise Car Show.
  D. Chamber Report: Ms. Califaux announced that the Chamber office has relocated to
  the office next to MK Stark and behind La Verne Construction.
  E. Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None
  F. Financial Report: Ms. Stark stated that a $15,000 transfer was requested to the
  Association account.

7  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:40 a.m., the annual meeting to be held on February 3,2025 at
  8:00 a.m. in the Quay-Davis Executive Board Room at the University of La Verne, 1950
  3'd Street, La Verne CA 91750.

  submitted,

  Natalie
